findings.title: Missing `minimal` value
findings.body: `reasoning_effort` only allows `"low"`, `"medium"` and `"high"`. GPT-5 models, which the tests target, also accept `"minimal"`, and the OpenAI SDK's `ReasoningEffort` type includes it. Because of the narrower `Literal`, `load_component` rejects `"minimal"` with a `ValidationError`, and type checkers flag it in the constructor. Consider adding `"minimal"` to the `Literal`, or reusing the SDK's `ReasoningEffort` type, in both `CreateArguments` and `CreateArgumentsConfigModel`.

findings.title: Type-check failures
findings.body:
The new tests are likely to fail strict pyright/mypy checks if those run on tests:
- The loop passes `valid_value`, inferred as `str`, to a parameter typed `Literal["low", "medium", "high"]`.
- `_create_args` and `_raw_config` are accessed on the result of `ChatCompletionClient.load_component`, which is typed as the base `ChatCompletionClient` and does not declare these attributes.

To fix, use explicit `Literal`-typed values or `cast`, load via `OpenAIChatCompletionClient.load_component` / `AzureOpenAIChatCompletionClient.load_component`, or narrow with `isinstance`.
